data.ruling: Refutation stands, scope function. The loop-delay entry, "TXD-to-RXD loop delay at most 237 ns", uses only DroneCAN's recommended 87.5 % sample point. The source it cites also gives the valid range at 1000 kbit/s as 75 % to 90 %, so any valid node on the port may sample at 75 %. During arbitration and ACK, a node that started the frame must see the far node's dominant bit before its own sample point. That needs loop(A) + loop(B) + 2 x 40 m x 5 ns/m <= SP(A). The entry keeps its own assumption that the remote transceiver equals the IO board's. With a remote at 75 %: (750 ns - 400 ns) / 2 = 175 ns. Two 237 ns loops plus the bus take 874 ns, over 750 ns, so a node meeting the entry can fail 40 m against a valid remote. The tree's own CAN timing samples at 75 % on the link: IOBoard.md:168-169, "both ends sample at 75 % of the bit". No line fixes the external port's sample point higher. The requirement is therefore at most 175 ns: about 3 ns less if both nodes' 0.3 m stubs are counted, and taken at 5 ns/m. The other entries (V18 to V21, V23 0 V, V24 +30 V, IOBoard.md:175, :192, rails, V7) were not disputed and are not ruled on here. The verifier's transceiver figures (TCAN3413DR 180 ns, TCAN1044VDRQ1 210 ns, TCAN1042HGVDRQ1 160/175 ns, TCAN1472VDRQ1 155/160 ns) were not re-read by this adjudicator. They are consequences for part selection, not the basis of this ruling.
data.evidence: DroneCAN "CAN bus parameters" table, re-read: "1000 kbit/s | 75% to 90% | 87.5% | 40 m | 0.3 m" (columns: bit rate, valid range for the sample point location, recommended location, max bus length, max stub length). Page text: "The estimated bus length limits are based on the assumption that the propagation delay does not exceed 5 ns/m, not including additional delay times of CAN transceivers and other components." Found V22 in FU-A1/004-P2-R2.json: "40 m total bus length at 1000 kbit/s, stubs at most 0.3 m, sample point 75 % to 90 %, 87.5 % recommended". The disputed entry's source, in the same file: "(875 ns to DroneCAN's recommended 87.5 % sample point - 2 x 40 m x 5 ns/m) / 2, the remote node taken as equal". Research.md:582 at e13f5f60: V22 answered "for research (owner, 2026-09-28)", with no owner figure for the sample point. IOBoard.md:168: "Bit timing | exactly 1 Mbit/s; both ends sample at 75 % of the bit". Arithmetic: (750 - 400) / 2 = 175 ns; 2 x 237 + 400 = 874 ns > 750 ns.
